  MINUTES
  Regular Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  Council Chambers, 111 South First Street
  April 8, 2024
  6:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL: At 6:08 p.m., on Monday, April 8, 2024, the Alhambra City Council met in the Council
Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  LEE, MALONEY, PÉREZ, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager
Stover, City Attorney Montes, City Clerk Myles, Director of Parks & Recreation Macias, Director of
Library Services LohGuan, Director of Public Works/Utilities Ray, Director of Finance Lieu, Director of
Human Resources Ko, Director of Community Development Ho, Police Chief Kennedy, Battalion Chief
Brown, Assistant Chief Fuentes

FLAG SALUTE:  Led by Mayor Maza

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledge that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take
care of each other.

CEREMONIALS

1.  PROCLAMATIONS – F2M24-3

  A.  The Alhambra City Councill ratified the action of Mayor Maza in proclaiming the month
  of April, 2024 as DONATE LIFE MONTH in Alhambra.

  B.  The Alhambra City Councill ratified the action of Mayor Maza in proclaiming April 24,
  2024 as DENIM DAY in Alhambra as a part of April being Sexual Assault Awareness
  Month.

2.  COMMENDATIONS: ALHAMBRA HIGH SCHOOL ACADEMIC DECATHLON TEAM –
  F2M24-3

  Mayor Maza and the Alhambra City Council wished to congratulate and commend the
  Alhambra High School 2024 Academic Decathlon Team for reaching the California State
  Academic Decathlon Competition. The Team took first place out of 63 teams in the 47th annual
  Los Angeles County Academic Decathlon after an outstanding performance in 10 subject
  areas. The Team’s victory led them to compete at the State level where they placed third

4-8-24  1
   among high school teams from across California, and were the first team from Alhambra High
  School to advance to the State level. The Team scored a total of more than 43,000 points and
  took home 18 medals. The AHS Academic Decathletes were to be commended for their
  perseverance and dedication to scholastic excellence and the City of Alhambra celebrates
  their accomplishments. Mayor Maza presented commendations to the AHS 2024 Academic
  Decathlon Team members and coach. The Team members were as follows:

  KENNETH SAN
  KEVIN SAN
  WILL SAN
  OSCAR DIAZ
  CLARISSA DIAZ
  RACHELLE LIU
  LYLA MEDINA
  CESAR GONZALEZ
  Coach JOSE SANCHEZ

  Mr. SANCHEZ commended his team and recounted their path to victory. Team Captain
  Kenneth SAN reported on the accomplishments of each team member from the competition.
  Mayor MAZA and the City Council offered their congratulations and commendation.

3.  COMMENDATION: ALHAMBRA ROTARY CLUB – DONATION OF BRONZE ART PIECE –
  F2M24-3

  Mayor Maza and the Alhambra City Council wished to commend the Alhambra Rotary Club
  for their generous donation of a bronze art piece displayed in front of the Alhambra Civic Center
  Library. The sculpture, depicting two children seated on a small bench enjoying a book,
  celebrates reading at all ages and commemorates the Alhambra Rotary Club’s 100th
  Anniversary. The Alhambra Rotary Club was founded in April of 1924 to fulfill the mission of
  the Rotary Club International organization to provide service to others, promote integrity, and
  advance world understanding, goodwill, and peace through their fellowship of business,
  professional, and community leaders. Over its long history, the Alhambra Rotary Club has not
  only instituted many of their own charitable events and programs, but has contributed their
  support to numerous City programs. The City of Alhambra was pleased to commend the
  Alhambra Rotary Club for their generosity and commitment to the betterment of the
  community. Mayor Maza presented the commendation to a representative of the Alhambra
  Rotary Club.

  Mayor MAZA thanked and commended the Alhambra Rotary Club for their work. Current
  Rotary President Greg CHEN offered Council and staff pins in commemoration of their 100th
  Anniversary. Ayla JEFFERSON, incoming Rotary President and Building Official for the City
  of Alhambra, provided background for the Rotary Club and their tests for determining projects.
  Council offered their gratitude and best wishes to the club.

PRESENTATIONS

4.  SAN GABRIEL BASIN WATER QUALITY AUTHORITY UPDATE – F2M24-16

  Mr. Robert GONZALES, Treasurer and Board Member representing cities with pumping rights,
  for the San Gabriel Basin Water Quality Authority provided an informational update to the City
  Council. Randy SCHOELLERMAN, Executive Director of the San Gabriel Basin WQA
  delivered a presentation, a copy of which is on file in the City Clerk’s office.

  2
4-8-24
   Public Comment:

  1) Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St. discussed the various agencies overseeing water
  control and the superfund site in Alhambra at Fremont and Mission. He continued to
  discuss water wells in Alhambra and potential clean up measures.

  2) Andrew LAU, 712 W. Ramona Rd., spoke regarding the importance of clean water.

  Discussion: Vice Mayor PÉREZ discussed Mr. McCammon’s comments and Mr.
  SCHOELLERMAN responded to questions regarding potential cleanup measures. They also
  discussed stored water levels and cleaning water for drinking water and coordination with the
  Environmental Protection Agency.

  Councilmember MALONEY discussed his time on the WQA as an alternate to Mr. Gonzales,
  and commended the WQA for their work.

  Councilmember LEE discussed the superfund site in Alhambra and Mr. SCHOELLERMAN
  responded to questions regarding the EPA investigation and feasibility study. They continued
  to discuss potential future developments near the site and environmental studies.

  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER and Mr. SCHOELLERMAN continued to discuss
  potential future developers and the cleanup of the superfund site. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER
  went on to discuss the background of the site.

  Mayor MAZA and Mr. SCHOELLERMAN continued to discuss the timeline for cleanup of the
  superfund site in Alhambra, potential funding sources for cleanup,

  Action Taken:  City Council received and filed this informational report.

5.  COUNCIL MEETING NORMS, PROCEDURES, AND DECORUM – F2M24-7

  At the March 11, 2024 City Council Meeting, Vice Mayor Pérez requested an agendized item
  regarding Council Meeting Norms, Procedures, and Decorum.

  Discussion:  Vice Mayor PÉREZ stated that after receiving information from staff,
  she would like to pull the item from discussion and continue it to a date uncertain.
  Councilmember LEE asked that the discussion move forward without any action taken. City
  Attorney MONTES clarified that this was requested by Council and that therefore Council could
  determine the discussion. Mayor MAZA supported continuing the item. Ms. LEE reiterated that
  she was willing to move forward with the discussion and that she would like to express
  concerns. Mr. MAZA allowed that he preferred to continue the discussion until additional
  information could be provided. Councilmember MALONEY and ANDRADE-STADLER agreed
  to continue the discussion and requested that Ms. Lee hold her comments until that time. Ms.
  LEE referred to the meeting on March 11, 2024 and questioned the Council’s willingness to
  debate rather than engage in personal attacks. She stated that if it was Council’s preference
  to continue the item, she would withhold her comments.

  Action Taken:  No action was taken.

CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 6 – 17)

All items listed under the Consent Agenda, with the exception of Item No. 6, were considered by the
City Council to be routine were enacted by one motion.

 6.  RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DIRECTOR AS
  APPROVING OFFICER FOR DETERMINATIONS OF PUBLIC CONVENIENCE OR
  NECESSITY FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGE CONTROL – F2M24-
  16, R2M24-11

  The State Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC) is responsible for administering
  licenses for the sale of alcoholic beverages. Pursuant to Section 23958 of the California
  Business and Professions Code, ABC shall deny an application for a license if issuance would
  result in or add to an undue concentration of licenses. Currently, the Alhambra Planning
  Commission was designated to make Public Convenience or Necessity (PCN) determinations
  regarding ABC license applications where undue concentration exists. The PCN finding was
  typically included as part of the Planning Commission Resolution approving any entitlement
  applications, such as a Conditional Use Permit, required for the ABC license. The adopted
  Planning Commission resolution would then be provided to ABC as the City’s formal PCN
  determination. With the recent adoption of the comprehensive Zoning Code update, certain
  ABC licenses, including Type 20 and 21 off-sale licenses, would no longer require Conditional
  Use Permits and therefore, would no longer require review by the Planning Commission.
  Consistent with the changes adopted as part of the Zoning Code update, staff recommened
  the City Council delegate to the Community Development Director the authority to make PCN
  determinations for ABC licenses, and delegate to the Community Development Director the
  authority to issue PCN letters after a determination is made.

  Discussion: Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER and Director of Community
  Development HO discussed the buffer zones around businesses approved for the sale of
  alcoholic beverages, the process for approval, and staff’s role.

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M24-11 entitled: A Resolution
  of the City Council of the City of Alhambra, California, designating the Community
  Development Director as the authority for determining Public Convenience or Necessity for
  the Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control, and authorizing the Community Development
  Director to issue Letters of Public Convenience or Necessity after a determination is made

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  PÉREZ
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, MALONEY, PÉREZ, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

7.  AUTHORIZE RFP: CITY HALL LOBBY ATTENDANT SERVICES – F2M20-43, RFP2M24-7

  The Lobby Attendant is responsible for directing City Hall visitors to the appropriate City
  Departments and/or personnel. The Lobby Attendant also conducts regular patrols of the City
  Hall and Library facilities, including parking structure, staircases, elevators, and adjacent court
  yards. At the close of business, the Lobby Attendant secures and locks the public entry and
  exit doors. The City contracted with A.G. Coast, Inc., DBA California Panther Security and the
  contract would terminate on June 30, 2024. Staff recommended the City Council authorize a
  request for proposals to ensure ongoing security support of City Hall facilities.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized staff to solicit proposals for Lobby Attendant
  services for Alhambra City Hall; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize
  Council’s action.

8.  AUTHORIZE RFP: PROFESSIONAL CONSULTANT SERVICES FOR THE HVAC DESIGN
  AT ALHAMBRA FIRE STATION 71 – F2M22-31, RFP2M24-9

  Fire Station 71 is headquarters for the Alhambra Fire Department. The existing HVAC system,
  which is the original 1966 design, is no longer capable of adequately and efficiently cooling
  and heating the building. In February 2023, a consultant was contracted to conduct a complete
  assessment of Fire Station 71. Based on the recommendations of the assessment of the
  existing HVAC equipment, staff sought City Council approval to solicit proposals for
  professional design services to redesign and replace the existing HVAC system.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized staff to solicit proposals for professional design
  services for Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) at Alhambra Fire Station 71,
  with proposals due no later than April 25, 2024; and, directed staff to undertake steps
  necessary to finalize Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA

9.  AWARD CONTRACT: ASBESTOS ABATEMENT AT THE FORMER LIBRARY SATELLITE
  BUILDING – 2025 SOUTH FREMONT AVENUE – F2M24-23, N2M24-20, C2M24-23, M2M24-
  53

  On February 12, 2024, the City Council approved the distribution of a Notice Inviting Bids for
  the Environmental Asbestos Abatement at the Former Library Satellite Building at 2025 South
  Fremont Avenue. This Project would include the removal of asbestos-containing materials
  such as roof mastic, duct mastic, and vinyl floor tiles. On March 14, 2024, the City Clerk
  received three bids for the Project. The bid received from Resource Environmental, Inc. was
  the lowest responsive bid.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to the final language
  approved by the City Manager and City Attorney, to Resource Environmental, Inc. in the
  amount of $22,000 for the Environmental Asbestos Abatement at the former Library Satellite
  building at 2025 South Fremont Avenue; and, directed staff to take the steps necessary to
  finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-53)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER

 10.  CONTRACT AMENDMENT: PARKING CITATION PROCESSING SERVICES – F2M20-29,
  C2M20-36, M2M24-54

  On August 10, 2020, City Council awarded a contract with Duncan Solutions dba Professional
  Account Management LLC for parking citation processing services for the period November 1,
  2020 through June 30, 2025 in an amount not to exceed $999,002.40. On February 28, 2022,
  the City Council approved a first contract amendment for an amount not to exceed
  $1,354,860.19 for the implementation of a virtual permitting system for annual and overnight
  parking. During the implementation process, staff proposed converting temporary permits to a
  virtual system, which was not initially budgeted for. The conversion required additional
  expenses of $89,827.18 to cover the Application Programming Interface (API) and
  convenience fees, which the City would cover during the duration of the contract.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved a Second Amendment, subject to final language
  approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, to the parking citation processing services
  agreement with Ducan Solutions dba Professional Account Management, LLC (C2M20-36)
  for an additional $89,827.18 in an amount not to exceed $1,444,687.37 through June 30, 2025;
  and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-54)

11.  AWARD CONTRACT: PURCHASE OF SELF-CONTAINED BREATHING APPARATUS
  (SCBA) – F2M24-6B, C2M24-20, M2M24-55

  The use of Self-Contained Breathing Apparatus (SCBA) is a required piece of Personal
  Protective Equipment (PPE), per the National Fire Protection Association. Wearing
  appropriate respiratory protection is essential for safety and well-being. The Alhambra Fire
  Department staff has used SCBAs that were 15 years old and exceeded their expected useful
  life. Staff sought to purchase new SCBAs through a cooperative purchase agreement. A
  cooperative purchase is allowable per Alhambra Municipal Code 3.36.080 section B3.
  Sourcewell awarded contract #032620-LNC to L.N. Curtis & Sons on May 5, 2020. Sourcewell
  bid specifications included an option for purchasing SCBAs, including related accessories and
  Personal Protective Equipment (PPE). Staff recommended purchasing the SCBAs utilizing this
  Sourcewell option.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to L. N. Curtis & Sons in an amount not to exceed
  $766,939.77 for the purchase of new Self-Contained Breathing Apparatus (SCBA) and
  accessories; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s
  action. (M2M24-55)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA

 12.  AWARD CONTRACT: PURCHASE OF RESCUE TOOLS FOR NEW FIRE DEPARTMENT
  TRUCK – F2M24-6B, C2M24-21, M2M24-56

  Western Extrication Specialists specializes in high-quality extrication tools, services, and
  training to customers. It was imperative that the Fire Department’s new truck is outfitted with
  fire and rescue equipment, technology, and the functional features of today’s fire trucks. The
  Fire Department’s apparatuses were outfitted with Holmatro rescue tools, which were
  interchangeable with the Holmatro tools that were being acquired. Maintaining the use of
  Holmatro tools would enhance compatibility, minimize errors, and reduce confusion during
  emergencies. It was important that all apparatuses be outfitted with comparable tools to
  ultimately improve the Fire Department’s ability to respond to emergencies. Pursuant to
  Alhambra Municipal Code 3.36.080 (B)(2), the purchase method may be dispensed when the
  equipment can only be obtained from one source (sole source). Therefore, staff recommended
  the City Council award a contract to Western Extrication Specialists, the sole Holmatro dealer
  for California, and waive the bid process.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and the City Attorney, to Western Extrication Specialists, Inc. for the
  purchase of rescue tools for the new fire truck, in an amount not to exceed $85,135.77; and,
  directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s action. (M2M24-56)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER

13.  CONTRACT AMENDMENT: PROFESSIONAL CONSULTING SERVICES FOR
  PREPERATION OF THE CITY’S OFFICIAL REPORTS FOR THE U.S. DEPARTMENT OF
  HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT (HUD) – F2M19-36, C2M22-49, M2M24-57

  In September 2022, the City Council awarded a contract to Veronica Tam & Associates for
  consulting and reporting related to the administration of the City’s Community Development
  Block Grant Funds (CDBG) and HOME Programs. The City has experienced a greater need
  for consulting support for a variety of other programming requirements including public notices,
  presentations to the HCDA Committee or the City Council, coordinating with the Los Angeles
  HUD Field Office, reporting under the Integrated Disbursement Information System (IDIS);
  consulting with other Departments on CDBG and HOME requirements, monitoring
  subrecipients for compliance, documentation, and other similar tasks as required for full
  program compliance. An estimated 104 hours were anticipated through the end of this Fiscal
  Year while another 416 hours are possible for Fiscal Year 2024-2025. Veronica Tam &
  Associates has a long history with Alhambra, and, therefore, has a strong understanding of
  the City’s housing and development needs and direction. Staff recommended the City Council
  authorize an Amendment to the contract with Veronica Tam & Associates to provide HUD
  consulting services for the City’s CDBG and HOME Programs, as needed.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved a contract amendment, subject to final language
  approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, by and between the City of Alhambra and
  Veronica Tam & Associates for additional professional services in the amount of $14,560 in
  FY 2023-24 and $60,320 in FY 2024-25 for a contract total not to exceed $201,180 for the
  preparation of the City of Alhambra’s Consolidated Plan, Annual Action Plan(s), Consolidated

   Annual Performance Report(s) (CAPER), the Analysis of Impediments to Fair Housing, and
  professional staff assistance; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize

14.  ADOPTION OF THE 2024 STRATEGIC PLAN – F2M24-33, M2M24-58

  The City Council, City Manager, Department Heads and Facilitator William Kelly of Kelly
  Associates Management Group held a Special Council Meeting for a Strategic Planning
  Session on March 13, 2024 to update the City’s current Strategic Plan (adopted in April 2023).
  Following the meeting, staff met to review the Council’s goals and objectives and discuss
  strategy and status of the new and updated strategic plan ideas with detailed goals and metrics
  to guide staff. On March 21, 2024, the City Council held a second special Council meeting to
  review all of the items on the updated 2024 Strategic Plan. The 2024 Strategic Plan contained
  six Goals, defined: Goal 1: Enhance Public Safety; Goal 2: Improve Infrastructure and Mobility;
  Goal 3: Create a Strong Financial Base and Strong Economic Base (Economic Development);
  Goal 4: Enhance Transparency and Open Governance; Goal 5: Promote Sustainability; and,
  Goal 6: Improve Housing Opportunities. Staff would bring updates on the 2024 Strategic Plan
  to the Council on a quarterly basis.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted the 2024 Strategic Plan and directed staff to
  undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-58)

17.  INITIATION OF THE PROCESS FOR THE CONDUCT OF THE NOVEMBER 5, 2024
  ALHAMBRA GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION – F2M24-38, O2M24-4829

  Staff requested the City Council consider adoption of an ordinance calling the General
  Municipal Election in the City of Alhambra to be held on November 5, 2024 to be consolidated
  with the Statewide General Election to be held that same date for the purpose of submitting to
  the qualified voters the following named officers: Councilperson of the Third District, full term
  and Councilperson of the Fourth District, full term; and, to take any and all actions necessary
  at this time to start the election process as more fully discussed in the City Clerk’s April 8,
  2024 report.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council declared introduced for its first reading the following
  ordinance entitled:

  Ordinance No. O2M24-4829: An Ordinance of the Alhambra City Council providing
  for a General Municipal Election in said city to be held on November 5, 2024 and
  providing for the consolidation of the General Municipal Election with the Statewide
  General Election, said election being held for the election of the following city officials,
  to wit: Councilperson of the Third District, full term; and, Councilperson of the Fourth
  District, full term

  which ordinance will return for a second reading and adoption at the next regular Council
  meeting.
